- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate during prolonged downward trends; adjust downward bias by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- Overshoot after price spikes (e.g., 2024-05-20, 2024-06-26) — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak observed in history.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lagged response: if true outcome is lower than forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2%.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility — if last 5 days show high variance, dampen forecast sensitivity to short-term noise.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 2–4% below forecast, shift model to use 28-day rolling average instead of 30-day.
